title: cam resume retry-monitor misclassification: stale retry.pid lifecycle, noop short-circuit ahead of recovery, false respawn promise
description: Three related defects around the retry-monitor pid in cam resume, all evidence-grounded during the CAM-426 spec interview (2026-07-26). (1) Stale pid file on the normal exit path: ~/.cam/retry.pid is written unconditionally by forkMonitor's onMonitorSpawned (src/commands/claude.ts:150, src/retry/launcher.ts:242) but cleanup (removeRetryPid) only fires on SIGINT/SIGTERM/SIGHUP (src/commands/claude.ts:151-155, src/retry/launcher.ts:257-259); when claude exits normally (/exit), runClaude returns without removing the file, leaving a permanent stale pid. No cam stop / cam prune path removes it either (src/commands/stop.ts cleans sidecar by argv only). (2) Pid-reuse misclassification blocks recovery: isRetryMonitorAlive (src/commands/resume.ts:246-250) treats ANY live pid as the monitor (isRetryPidAlive even counts EPERM as alive, src/util/retry-pid.ts:92-96); classifyResumeMode short-circuits to noop at the third branch, AHEAD of the live-supervisor and orphaned-worker checks (src/commands/resume.ts:315-320), so cam resume refuses to recover anything while pointing at an unrelated recycled pid. test/resume.test.ts:274-275,388 encode this precedence as intended, so the suite will never flag it. (3) The noop hint lies even with a healthy monitor: 'retry-monitor will respawn cam next when the rate-limit window ends' (src/commands/resume.ts:642-647) promises a respawn the monitor never performs; the monitor only types config.retryMessage into a tmux pane (src/retry/monitor.ts:116-119). Fix directions to evaluate at spec time: remove retry.pid on the normal exit path of runClaude; make liveness verification argv-aware (match the retry-monitor command line, not bare pid liveness) mirroring stop.ts's sidecar approach; demote or re-order the noop branch below supervisor/worker recovery checks; make the hint text honest. SEQUENCING: spec this against post-CAM-426 reality: once CAM-426 ships, the monitor actually lives on compiled binaries, which changes the character of the stale-pid hazard (live monitors become the common case, normal-exit leaks remain). Kept separate from CAM-426 by fix-site policy (resume.ts/claude.ts lifecycle vs the self-invoke primitive).
